synthesis.paragraph: Three papers carry the tag "Geographic Information Systems Studies," focusing on automated quality assessment of geospatial vector data, using individual GIS projects to build student self-efficacy, and standardising warnings and hazard maps in Germany's natural hazards portal. Another three papers are grouped under "Urban Green Space and Health," which estimate urban vertical greenery potential, enhance heatwave resilience in recreational public spaces, and integrate the public realm into the urban fabric of Middle Eastern cities. The tag "interview" also covers three of today's papers, which study the integration of the public realm in Doha, use individual GIS projects to build student self-efficacy, and examine vertical ethnoburbs in Melbourne. Outside these groups, one paper quantifies the ecological decline of an urban tropical wetland ecosystem in India using multi-temporal satellite imagery, another evaluates the spatial reasoning of large language models for the discrete p-median problem, and a third models crowd-shippers' behavioral decisions using a covariate-dependent choice model.
